newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First confirms all utilities on restricted list.
newsitem.headline: NZ First confirms all utilities on restricted list.

text.p: Opposition New Zealand First leader Winston Peters on Wednesday listed the strategic assets over which he would restrict foreign ownership and confirmed all electricity and gas companies were included.
In August Peters released the party's policy restricting foreign ownership in strategic assets to 24.9 percent.
All those with larger levels of foreign ownership would be able to keep their shareholding but would only be able to on-sell to New Zealand-owned businesses or individuals.

At the time he gave an indicative list which included "telecommunications, utilities (such as electricity and gas companies) ports, transport companies of national importance like Air New Zealand and so on".
He said he would issue "a full list" of the assets covered by the policy before the election.
After requests for details by Reuters, Peters released a statement which added little to the original policy list but firmed up the restriction on gas and electricity utilities.

A spokeman for Peters said the policy would apply to "all utilities, electricity and gas companies, Air New Zealand the national flag carrier, port and airport companies, all current State Owned Enterprises, all companies with effective market monopolies, (Telecom is an example) and Forestry Corporation."

The government sold Forestry Corporation to a consortium led by Fletcher Forest for a net NZ$1.6 billion in August but Peters has said if his party was in power after the October 12 election it would repurchase the corporation.
Peters said all government-owned entities and assets would remain under 100 percent state ownership. There would be no further asset sales.
New Zealand First is averaging 15 percent support in opinion polls and is almost certain to be part of either a centre-left or centre-right government after Saturday's election.
But neither the ruling National Party nor the main opposition Labour Party supports his foreign ownership policy.
